Hi Alice — thanks for the list. Answers below and I’ve attached the three docs referenced in Rishi’s note.

SOC 2
- Report type: SOC 2 Type II (security). Reporting period: 2024-01-01 through 2024-12-31.
- Scope: hosted Redwood API + control plane telemetry; Dedicated pools are included in system description where they are Redwood-managed. For dedicated customer-managed deployments we provide a controls mapping; we can clarify for Private/VPC on a case-by-case basis.

HIPAA / BAA
- We support HIPAA workloads in Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem) and offer a standard BAA. We do not ingest PHI into hosted multitenant environments by default; any HIPAA work is done under specific configuration and contract terms.

Pen test / VAPT
- Last full third-party pen test: 2025-11-02. Vendor: AcmeSec (third-party).
- Scope: external network perimeter and customer-facing application layer, authenticated web testing included for core API endpoints and console flows. Internal-only pentests are performed for major infra changes and upon request for private deployments.
- Redacted summary: attached (pen-test-redacted-summary-2025.pdf). Full report: available under mutual NDA + evidence access agreement. Typical turnaround to provide full report after contracts are signed is 2–5 business days (we redact any customer-identifying info where necessary).

Vulnerability management / SLAs
- Scanning cadence: weekly authenticated scans (internal SAST/DAST + dependency checks), daily external unauthenticated surface scans, monthly container image scans, continuous dependency monitoring in CI.
- Remediation SLA targets (internal goal):
   • Critical (RCE/critical auth bypass): mitigation or compensating control within 72 hours; full engineering patch tracked and prioritized for immediate release.
   • High: mitigation/workaround within 24–72 hours, patch within 7 days.
   • Medium: fix within 30 days or tracked in product backlog with acceptable compensating controls.
   • Low: tracked and scheduled per product roadmap.
- Exceptions & escalation: we have an internal Security Incident Response process and customer notification path; critical issues trigger immediate notification within 24 hours.

Coordinated disclosure
- We follow a coordinated disclosure policy for vulnerabilities: standard window is 90 days to remediation before public disclosure unless critical and customer-impacting (in which case we notify affected customers immediately and share mitigations). We will provide Acme with our disclosure policy and process map.

Attachments (stubs):
- Attachment: Redwood-SOC2-TypeII-Statement-2024.pdf (application/pdf, 260 KB)
- Attachment: pen-test-redacted-summary-2025.pdf (application/pdf, 180 KB)
- Attachment: vuln-mgmt-process-summary.pdf (application/pdf, 45 KB)
